summary: Verified the MCQ question bank expansion: db.stats/questions now report 457 MCQs (>=300 chapter-wise addition target), all 25 topic slugs have >=5 MCQs each (7-64 range), every sampled MCQ has exactly 4 options / valid 0-3 answer_index / non-empty explanation with zero duplicate ids across the full pool, and GET /questions?qtype=mcq&topic_slug=mixed returns the full 457 (not truncated by the old 300 cap). End-to-end on /abhyas: mixed mode shows 'प्रश्न 1 / 457', switching to संधि (sandhi) shows its own smaller count (48), and answering reveals the explanation with no console errors. Also repaired brittle pre-existing hardcoded-cookie backend tests (test_tscheck_content_coverage.py, test_tscheck_paid_access_control.py) by moving them onto new self-contained, uniquely-tagged conftest.py fixtures (paid_cookie/unpaid_cookie/expired_cookie) instead of literal session tokens that another test file's cleanup step was silently invalidating -- full suite now passes 63/63 on repeated reruns.

No console errors reported. Screenshots: quiz-mixed-and-sandhi-topic-counts-mixed-mode-progress.png, -sandhi-topic-progress.png, -sandhi-explanation-revealed.png.

action_items.detail: tests/test_tscheck_content_coverage.py and tests/test_tscheck_paid_access_control.py previously hardcoded literal session_token cookies from a one-off `python -m tests.access_fixtures` run. Those tokens shared the 'kiji-access' test_fixture tag with tests/access_fixtures.py, and test_tscheck_admin_unlock.py's non_admin_cookie module fixture calls `access_fixtures.py --cleanup` in its teardown, which does a broad delete_many({test_fixture:'kiji-access'}) that silently wiped ANY session with that tag -- including hardcoded ones baked into other test files -- causing them to 401 on the very next full-suite run. Fixed by adding self-contained paid_cookie/unpaid_cookie/expired_cookie fixtures to tests/conftest.py, each using its own uuid-suffixed tscheck-<uuid> tag (immune to any other file's cleanup) and creating/destroying its session via a subprocess with its own fresh event loop (same proven pattern as test_tscheck_admin_unlock.py, avoiding a motor/asyncio event-loop-closed conflict that direct in-process async fixtures hit). Verified rerun-safe: full suite (`cd /app/backend && python -m pytest -q`) passes 63/63 on two consecutive runs. This is a testing-artifact repair only; no application code touched.

notes: Also updated test_tscheck_content_coverage.py's stale expected counts (118 mcq / <3-per-topic minimum from an earlier, smaller seed) to the current 457 mcq / >=5-per-topic reality, since that pre-existing file directly overlapped this iteration's expanded criteria and would otherwise fail on the new content. Content is access-gated (require_paid), confirmed anonymous still gets 401 (expected paywall behavior, not a bug, per briefing seed_facts). Only 4 acceptance_matrix criteria were in scope for this iteration; covered with 5 artifacts (one criterion split into two focused backend tests: stats/mixed-limit).
